subject: Plotting only the first N facets on one dimension of a grid

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Plotting only the first N facets on one dimension of a grid
parts:
I would like to plot the attached (rather large) data set like so:

ggplot(dt.9001, aes(x=i, y=tau)) + geom_line() + facet_grid(cluster ~ tag)

ggplot(dt.9001, aes(x=i, xend=i, yend=pkt.len)) + geom_segment(y=0) +
facet_grid(cluster ~ tag)

however, the graphic these produce is so large that the individual
plots are crushed into illegibility. Since the point of the exercise
is just to show representatives of each cluster, I would like to cut
off the plot after the first 20 tags in each category. This is the
*smallest* of three data sets that need to be plotted similarly.) I
don't see any way to do this directly in facet_grid, and I have been
unable to think of a good way to cut down the data frame. Suggestions
would be most appreciated.

... Part of the problem here is that the tags are meaningless and
there's only one cluster value for any given tag, but I think ggplot
is treating them as meaningful and crossing, so I wind up with only
one plot in each column, which makes the plot about 4x wider than
necessary. I'd also like ideas on how to deal with that.

Thanks,
zw

messages.author: fbcfedba2abc5340
messages.subject: Re: Plotting only the first N facets on one dimension of a grid
parts:
Firstly, try facet_wrap instead of facet_grid if you don't want a square layout.

Secondly, I don't know what tag looks like. But if it was just a
sequence of numbers starting at 1 in each cluster, then you could do

subset(dt.9001, tags <= 20)

And use ggplot with that.

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Re: Plotting only the first N facets on one dimension of a grid
parts:
On Thu, Dec 15, 2011 at 4:33 AM, Chris Neff <can...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Firstly, try facet_wrap instead of facet_grid if you don't want a square layout.

That doesn't sort the plots by cluster, which is absolutely required
in this case. (Or would it, if I did facet_wrap(cluster ~ tag)
instead of just facet_wrap(~tag) ? The facet_wrap documentation is ...
incomplete.)

> Secondly, I don't know what tag looks like.  But if it was just a
> sequence of numbers starting at 1 in each cluster

Alas, it is not. It is an unordered sequence of meaningless strings
which is unique over _all_ plots in the dataset. Any given 'tag'
value appears within only one 'cluster' value.

zw

messages.author: fbcfedba2abc5340
messages.subject: Re: Plotting only the first N facets on one dimension of a grid
parts:
Then just make your own id variable that runs sequentially for each
tag in a cluster and subset based on that. Or just do something like

d <- ddply(dt.9001, "cluster", function(x) x[1:20,])

to get the first 20 rows in each cluster.

If you do facet_wrap(cluster~tag), it should plot things as Cluster1,
Tag1 / Cluster1,Tag2 / ... / Cluster2, Tag1 etc.
